title: How a Fashion House Transfers Tacit Knowledge
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A house transfers tacit knowledge by pairing records with situated practice: demonstration, attempt, correction, comparison, narration, and trusted authority. The goal is not to extract every secret, but to preserve what collaborators may ethically carry.
The ensemble carries material decisions across components; the surviving object cannot narrate every demonstration, correction, and embodied judgment that produced them.

01 · SHOW — What must be demonstrated?. Identify judgments that resist prose: hand position, tension, sequence, sound, resistance, drape, finishing threshold, and the moment an expert stops. Record only with informed permission.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · TRY — Where does the learner practice?. Design a bounded attempt using sacrificial material, time for repetition, and permission to fail. Apprenticeship is labor and education; compensation, safety, access, and jurisdiction must be addressed.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · CORRECT — How is judgment calibrated?. Preserve paired examples, expert commentary, acceptable variation, non-negotiable failure, and the reason for correction. Record disagreement instead of forcing false consensus.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · RETURN — Who retains authority over the knowledge?. Define consent, attribution, confidentiality, access, benefit, revocation, cultural authority, archive custody, and successor permissions. Not all knowledge should become a company asset or public lesson.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

With consent, record demonstration, learner attempt, correction, acceptable variation, and stop condition.
Attach contributor, compensation, confidentiality, cultural-authority, access, archive, and revocation terms.
Have the practitioner and, where appropriate, a cultural specialist approve the description before publication.
